summary_of_change:
In stark contrast to bear thesis assumptions, Broadcom's operational engine continues to accelerate across its core semiconductor and infrastructure software divisions. Across the latest four consecutive quarters (Q4 FY25 to Q3 FY26), quarterly revenue progressed rapidly from $18.0B to $19.1B, $22.2B, and reached a record $29.59B in Q3 FY26 (+85.5% YoY), establishing a real-time annualized revenue run-rate of $118.36B. Forward management guidance for Q4 FY26 projects revenue of approximately $34.8B (+93% YoY), powered by custom AI accelerator (XPU) volume ramps including Google's TPU v8i and Meta's MTIA scaling alongside Tomahawk 6 / Jericho 3 AI Ethernet switching silicon.

Simultaneously, the Infrastructure Software segment is generating record cash flows following the VMware acquisition. Software revenue reached $8.8B in Q3 FY26 (+29% YoY), driven by the rapid conversion of the top 20,000 sovereign cloud and large enterprise customers to VMware Cloud Foundation (VCF) multi-year subscription bundles. Software non-GAAP operating margins expanded toward 79%, while consolidated gross margins remained pristine at 78.6% and non-GAAP operating margins expanded to 67.9%.

Broadcom's fabless, asset-light operating model required just $532M in Q3 CapEx (<1.8% of revenue), converting 46.3% of revenue into $13.7B of quarterly free cash flow ($14.2B operating cash flow). On capital allocation, management continues to prioritize post-VMware debt reduction, bringing net balance sheet debt down to $41.0B ($-8.78 per share), while returning $3.1B quarterly through dividends ($0.65/share quarterly dividend) and maintaining disciplined cash allocation.

How Things Are Going Now

In stark contrast to bear thesis assumptions, Broadcom's operational engine continues to accelerate across its core semiconductor and infrastructure software divisions. Across the latest four consecutive quarters (Q4 FY25 to Q3 FY26), quarterly revenue progressed rapidly from $18.0B to $19.1B, $22.2B, and reached a record $29.59B in Q3 FY26 (+85.5% YoY), establishing a real-time annualized revenue run-rate of $118.36B. Forward management guidance for Q4 FY26 projects revenue of approximately $34.8B (+93% YoY), powered by custom AI accelerator (XPU) volume ramps including Google's TPU v8i and Meta's MTIA scaling alongside Tomahawk 6 / Jericho 3 AI Ethernet switching silicon.

Simultaneously, the Infrastructure Software segment is generating record cash flows following the VMware acquisition. Software revenue reached $8.8B in Q3 FY26 (+29% YoY), driven by the rapid conversion of the top 20,000 sovereign cloud and large enterprise customers to VMware Cloud Foundation (VCF) multi-year subscription bundles. Software non-GAAP operating margins expanded toward 79%, while consolidated gross margins remained pristine at 78.6% and non-GAAP operating margins expanded to 67.9%.

Broadcom's fabless, asset-light operating model required just $532M in Q3 CapEx (<1.8% of revenue), converting 46.3% of revenue into $13.7B of quarterly free cash flow ($14.2B operating cash flow). On capital allocation, management continues to prioritize post-VMware debt reduction, bringing net balance sheet debt down to $41.0B ($-8.78 per share), while returning $3.1B quarterly through dividends ($0.65/share quarterly dividend) and maintaining disciplined cash allocation.
